user.title: Vimar Intercom
user.description: Add the Vimar Elvox video intercom. The SIP credentials are inside the pairing QR code: with the QR you don't need to type them.

qr.title: Scan pairing QR code
qr.description: Paste the text of the pairing QR code (the one the intercom or the VIEW app shows): read it with a QR scanner app and paste what it shows, not a photo. On error: {error_detail}

data_description.qr_text: One long encoded (Base64) string, exactly as the QR scanner shows it. It holds the SIP password: don't use an online decoder.

manual.title: SIP credentials
manual.description: Only if you can't use the QR: these are the values inside the decoded pairing QR code (ID, PWD, DOMAIN, CPROXY).

data_description.sip_user: The credential's SIP ID (ID in the decoded QR): the place Home Assistant takes on the intercom.
data_description.sip_password: The credential's SIP password (PWD in the decoded QR; the QR text does not show it in clear).
data_description.sip_domain: The credential's SIP domain (DOMAIN in the decoded QR; if it is 127.0.0.1, as on a 40515, use CDOMAIN). Not the cloud proxy.
data_description.cloud_proxy: The cloud SIP proxy (CPROXY in the decoded QR). Default: ipvdes.vimar.cloud.

network.title: Local network
network.description: Enter the local IP of the intercom. Plant: {plant}. Setup registers for real on the expected transport and, if that fails, tries the other one (local UDP or cloud TLS) and keeps whichever works. User: {sip_user}@{sip_domain}, MAC: {mac}. On error: {error_detail}

data_description.local_proxy: The local IP address of your Vimar intercom (e.g. 192.168.1.100).
data_description.use_local_udp: Preset from the plant type in the QR. Due Fili Plus EVO plants only deliver calls through the cloud relay; if the first path fails, the other one is tried.
data_description.local_udp_port: UDP port used by HA for local SIP. Default: 5060.
data_description.device_name: The name the integration shows the intercom (MyName header). The pairing binds it to the credential: do not change it once registered.

zeroconf_confirm.title: Vimar intercom found on the network
zeroconf_confirm.description: Home Assistant found a Vimar intercom at {host} (MAC {mac}, model {model}, firmware {firmware}). To connect it you still need the pairing QR code or the SIP credentials: the address and the local domain are already filled in.

zeroconf_moved.title: Has the intercom changed address?
zeroconf_moved.description: The configured Vimar intercom announced itself at {new} instead of {old}. Confirm only if you moved it or your router gave it a new address: anyone on the local network can announce its MAC. On confirmation Home Assistant uses {new} and reloads the integration.

reconfigure.title: New pairing QR
reconfigure.description: Paste the text of the new QR the intercom created for Home Assistant (read it with a QR app and paste what it shows, not a photo). Only the SIP credentials change: entities, automations, options and network settings stay as they are (the transport changes only if the QR works solely on the other one, and you are told). Before saving, the QR is tried with a real registration. If it fails: {error_detail}

data_description.qr_text: One long encoded string (Base64), exactly as the QR reader shows it. It contains the SIP password: do not use online decoders.

error.invalid_device_name: Invalid name: 1 to 64 printable characters, no control characters.
error.sip_registration_failed: SIP registration failed over both local UDP and cloud TLS. Check that the intercom IP is right and reachable from HA, and that the credentials are the QR's (domain included).

abort.no_mac: The intercom announced itself without a MAC: add it by hand from Settings → Devices & services.
abort.single_instance_allowed: Vimar Intercom is already set up: only one installation is supported.
abort.reconfigure_successful: Credentials updated: the integration reloads with the new QR.
abort.reconfigure_transport_changed: Credentials updated, but the new QR works only on the other transport (local UDP or cloud TLS): the integration now uses that one and reloads. The detail is in the Home Assistant log.

create_entry.transport_fallback: Home Assistant could not register over {tried} and uses {used} instead: {detail}. It works, but if you expected {tried}, check the intercom's network settings.

internal_panel.title: Find indoor monitor
internal_panel.description: The system declares the PICG {detected}. The current Call Home target is {current}. The declared PICG is proposed as the indoor monitor, also when it is the same as the SGA: on the plants tried it is the address that rings the monitor. Confirm the target or enter the known address of an indoor monitor. Saving does not start a call.

settings.title: Vimar Intercom settings
settings.description: SIP network and dynamic actuators. In the Actuators field paste the JSON list produced by tools/parse_rubrica.py, or go back to the menu and use "Import actuators from rubrica.db".

data.camera_target: Video entrance panel (SIP id to call)
data.internal_panel_target: Internal panel (SIP id for “Call the indoor monitor”)
data.door_target: Entrance panel that opens the door
data.away_message_upload: Or upload the audio file (mp3, wav, m4a)
data.away_message_text: Message if nobody answers (text, read by TTS)
data.away_message_delay: After how many seconds of ringing (used only if the Tab does not expose the voicemail delay; 0 = 20 s)
data.snapshot_delay: Seconds for the better snapshot (0 = first only)
data.view_keepalive: Seconds of silence for “Vedi esterno” (0 = none)
data.allowed_users: Users allowed to see rings and live media (empty = everyone)

data_description.voice_answer: Who can answer the call by talking while it rings. Declared only: only connections using /audio_ws?voice_answer=1 (Echo Show, HomeKit via Scrypted). Never: talking never answers. Anyone: any connection with a microphone can answer; beware, a wall tablet whose microphone was left open can answer by itself with household noise.
data_description.media_enc: Automatic: follows what the system declares in its GET_INIT_STATUS reply ("media_enc": "srtp" on a cloud Tab 5S Up 40515); when the system does not declare it (short reply, as on the 40507) media stays plain. On/Off force it. If the camera stays black or the call fails with 488, try On.
data_description.video_enabled: On by default. Turn it off for entrance panels without a camera, whose calls then stay audio only. The pairing QR's VIDEO field does not change it: in the Vimar apps it only allows the preview while it rings.
data_description.actuators: JSON list of objects name, msg, target, icon. icon: door|light|switch. target "AUTO" uses the panel that opens the door. Empty = no buttons.
data_description.sga_target: Target for VOICEMAIL;/DND;, and for the door-open command when “Entrance panel that opens the door” is empty. Empty = historical default (55001). Change it only if your system uses a different SGA (SYSTEM.MAGIC_APT_INTERCOM in rubrica.db).
data_description.picg_target: Target for GET_INIT_STATUS. On systems verified so far it matches the SGA. Empty = historical default (55001).
data_description.camera_target: Panel called by the camera, by “Call” and by “Call the entrance panel (video)”: the PHONEBOOK row with TYPE='PE' in rubrica.db (the phonebook import fills it in). Empty = the panel learned from the last ring with video, else 55100. This is not the SGA.
data_description.internal_panel_target: Target of the “Call the indoor monitor” button. Empty = the apartment's PICG (the GET_INIT_STATUS target), which rings the indoor monitor on the plants tried. Use “Find indoor monitor” to propose it, or enter a known address.
data_description.door_target: Where the door-open command goes: the GID_PE of the door actuator in the phonebook (on a 2FV2 it is not the SGA). Filled in by importing or downloading the phonebook. Empty = the door actuator's panel if actuators were imported, otherwise the SGA.
data_description.away_message_file: Audio file (mp3, wav...) played to the visitor when nobody answers, e.g. /config/media/citofono/messaggio.mp3 (or pick the file on the device page: upload it from Media > Local media > citofono/messaggi). Empty = off.
data_description.away_message_upload: The file goes to media folder/citofono/messaggi and becomes the away message right away. Max 5 MB; if a different file with the same name is already there, this one gets -2 added.
data_description.away_message_text: Text read to the visitor by Home Assistant's text-to-speech when the file field is empty (the file takes precedence). In HA's language, max 30 s of audio. Empty = off.
data_description.away_message_tts: TTS entity that reads the text (e.g. tts.google_translate_en_com, tts.piper). Empty = HA's default TTS engine. If synthesis fails the doorbell keeps ringing as usual.
data_description.away_message_delay: If it is still ringing after this many seconds (nobody answered from the panel, phone or HA), the integration answers, plays the file and hangs up. If the Tab exposes the delay (Voicemail delay) that one is used; this value only matters when the Tab does not expose it. 0 = 20 s.
data_description.snapshot_dir: Folder where the visitor's snapshot (squillo_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_mmm.jpg and ultimo_squillo.jpg) and the ring clip (.mp4, up to 60 s) are saved, e.g. /config/media/citofono. Must be in allowlist_external_dirs or a media folder. Empty = do not save.
data_description.snapshot_delay: The first snapshot is saved as soon as the first frame arrives (~1 s after the ring); after this many seconds it is replaced by a frame with the exposure settled (the panel's first one is dark). 3 s suits the Tab 5S Up 40515; increase it if snapshots come out dark, 0 = keep the first.
data_description.view_keepalive: While viewing the outside the integration sends audio silence; without it, over the cloud the panel closes the view after ~10 s. It stops this many seconds after the view starts (the view then ends by itself). On the 2-wire plant in local mode the silence keeps the apartment busy: the default is 0 in local mode and 120 over the cloud; 0 = no silence (on the 2-wire use 0 or 30).
data_description.allowed_users: Limits the card, the ring history (photos and clips) and /audio_ws to these Home Assistant users. Admins always. Empty = every logged-in user. It does NOT limit the camera entity or /av from the local network: anyone who can open the camera sees (and hears) the stream; and if the photo folder is under an HA media directory, photos and clips show up in the media browser for every user.
data_description.ring_webhook_url: GET (fire-and-forget) sent when a ring starts, e.g. to turn on a dummy switch (Scrypted Dummy Switch) linked to a Custom Doorbell Button. A failure is only logged as a warning and never stops the ring. Empty = off.
data_description.ring_end_webhook_url: GET (fire-and-forget) sent when the ring ends, answered, cancelled or timed out: same idea as above, to turn the switch off. Empty = off.
data_description.video_bandwidth: Applies to every video from the panel: the card, the camera, /av and HomeKit. Automatic (recommended): 2 Mbit/s on local UDP, 256 kbit/s over the cloud relay, which loses a few packets in a hundred. 256 kbit/s: a lighter stream, fewer damaged frames on a lossy relay, but a smaller picture on some panels (a Tab 5S Up 40515 drops to 320x240 at 15 fps). 2 Mbit/s: the sharpest picture (720x576 at 24 fps on a 40515) and ten times the traffic; on a relay that loses packets (measured on a Tab 7S Up 40517) the video smears, freezes and lags.

homekit.title: HomeKit video doorbell
homekit.description:
Publish the intercom to the Apple Home app as a video doorbell: ring notification, live video, two-way audio and the gate in the same view.

Whoever pairs it (and everyone the home is shared with in the Home app) sees the video, talks and opens the gate: Home Assistant's allowed users option does not apply to HomeKit.

Do not also pair the same intercom through a Scrypted HomeKit bridge: the Home app would show two doorbells and every ring would notify twice.

{pairing}

data_description.homekit_accessory: Turns on the HomeKit video doorbell. Until it is paired, the setup code and the QR code to scan with the Home app appear above; a notification says that pairing is waiting. After 10 wrong codes in a row the code changes.
data_description.homekit_video_smooth: On (recommended): Home Assistant re-encodes the panel's video with a keyframe every second, so a packet lost on the cloud relay shows as a brief smear instead of a freeze. Opening takes about half a second longer and uses some CPU. Off: the video goes straight to the phone and opens faster, but a lost packet can freeze the picture for up to 3 seconds.
data_description.homekit_answer: Answer when you talk: opening the notification shows and plays the street without answering, so the Tab and the app can still answer; your first word (Talk) answers. Answer when the view opens: opening the notification answers at once and the Tab stops ringing.
data_description.homekit_ring_button: Adds a programmable button that is pressed at every ring, to use as a trigger in Home app automations. Off: one tile less in the Home app; the ring notification, video, Talk and the gate are unchanged.

import_rubrica.title: Import from rubrica.db
import_rubrica.description: Upload the rubrica.db file extracted from the system (see docs/RUBRICA.md): the integration automatically derives your apartment's actuators, without manually copying the output of tools/parse_rubrica.py. The file is read read-only and is not kept by Home Assistant after import. {rubrica_error}

data_description.rubrica_gid: The apartment's GID in the phonebook (usually the one already in use, e.g. 101).

import_confirm.title: Confirm import

fetch_rubrica.title: Download from the intercom
fetch_rubrica.description:
Asks the intercom ({host}) for the phonebook directly, using the SIP credentials already configured: no manual extraction and no Vimar account needed. The same request also asks for the PICG, which the intercom reports itself.

This works when the intercom is reachable on the local network; if it does not answer, use "Import actuators from rubrica.db". {rubrica_error}

data_description.rubrica_gid: The apartment GID in the phonebook (usually the one already in use, e.g. 101).

fetch_rubrica_cloud.title: Download from the Vimar cloud
fetch_rubrica_cloud.description: Downloads the phonebook from {cproxy} with the token the system sends in its GET_INIT_STATUS reply: it is the same rubrica.db file the VIEW app uses. Only for systems that send the long reply (seen on a Tab 5S Up 40515 / 2FV2); the token is not stored. {rubrica_error}

data_description.rubrica_gid: The apartment GID in the phonebook (the one the system declares is proposed).

av_key.title: /av stream key
av_key.description:
`/api/vimar_intercom/av` without `autocall=0` calls the panel: it only accepts an authenticated Home Assistant user or this key in the `{param}` parameter. The integration's camera adds it by itself.

Current key: `{key}`

For go2rtc, Frigate or Scrypted append `&{param}=` followed by the key to the URL (see docs/EXTERNAL.md). On passive URLs (`autocall=0`) it is optional for now, but a wrong key is refused.

If a log or a URL with the key ever reached someone else, regenerate it: the old key stops working at once and the integration reloads (a call in progress drops).

data_description.regenerate: Creates a new key. Then update the URL in go2rtc, Frigate or Scrypted, if they use it.

error.invalid_actuator_target: Invalid actuator target ({actuators_error}): digits only (e.g. 55001) or AUTO.
error.rubrica_import_failed: Import failed. See description above for details.
error.rubrica_no_actuators: No actuators found for GID {rubrica_gid}: check the apartment GID.
error.internal_panel_not_found: The nickname reply does not declare a unique valid PICG. Enter a known indoor monitor address manually.
error.internal_panel_no_reply: No nickname reply arrived from the configured PICG. Some cloud plants do not answer GET_NICKS even at an existing address. This does not prove the address is wrong; enter a known indoor monitor address manually.
error.internal_panel_unavailable: The nickname lookup could not run: the integration may be disconnected or another search may be in progress. Retry once it is available, or enter a known indoor monitor address manually.
error.invalid_url: Invalid URL: it must start with http:// or https:// and have a host.
error.no_local_proxy: The intercom address is missing: set it under "Network and actuator settings".
error.rest_auth_failed: The intercom rejected the SIP credentials, or does not expose this API. Note: it answers 401 in both cases.
error.rest_unavailable: The intercom is not reachable over HTTP on the local network. If the system only works through the cloud, use “Download the phonebook from the Vimar cloud” or the file import instead.
error.file_not_allowed: File outside the folders Home Assistant may read: add its folder to allowlist_external_dirs or use a media folder.
error.text_too_long: Text too long: 255 characters at most.
error.file_not_found: File not found: use the full path, e.g. /config/media/citofono/messaggio.mp3.
error.upload_bad_type: Upload an .mp3, .wav or .m4a file with a plain name (letters, digits, spaces, - _ . ( )).
error.upload_failed: File not saved in the messages folder: see the Home Assistant log.
error.path_not_allowed: Home Assistant cannot write to this folder: add it to allowlist_external_dirs or use a media folder.
error.path_public: Public folder: /config/www is served on /local without login. Use e.g. /config/media/citofono.
error.no_cloud_token: The status reply did not include a phonebook token. Use the intercom download or import rubrica.db instead.
error.no_cloud_status: No status reply was received. Check that the integration is connected and that the PICG address is correct, then retry. This does not establish whether the system supports cloud phonebook downloads.
error.cloud_auth_failed: The Vimar cloud rejected the token.
error.cloud_failed: Phonebook download from the cloud failed.
error.actuators_bad_json: Invalid actuators list: not valid JSON ({actuators_error})
error.actuators_not_list: Invalid actuators list: it must be a JSON list, [ ... ]
error.actuators_not_object: Invalid actuators list: item {actuators_error} is not a JSON object
error.actuators_missing_keys: Invalid actuators list: missing keys in item {actuators_error} (needed: name, msg, target, icon)
error.actuators_bad_icon: Invalid actuators list: icon not allowed in item {actuators_error} (allowed: door, light, switch)
error.cloud_missing_data: Phonebook download from the cloud not possible: missing {cloud_missing} (the cloud domain and proxy come from the QR code).

send_command.name: Send SIP command
send_command.description: Send an arbitrary SIP MESSAGE to the intercom (for testing commands).

call.name: Call
call.description: Start a call to an entry panel or monitor.

decline.name: Decline
decline.description: Decline the incoming call (603): the whole house stops ringing.

simulate_ring.name: Test ring
simulate_ring.description: Simulate a whole ring with no entrance panel and no SIP traffic: ringing state (card, sensors), doorbell event and start webhook, then it ends by itself like an unanswered ring (end webhook).

duration.name: Duration
duration.description: Seconds of ringing before it ends by itself.

open_door.name: Open door
open_door.description: Send the door-open command to the entry panel.

target.name: Entry panel
target.description: Entry panel SIP ID. Empty = the panel that opens the door (from the phonebook), otherwise the SGA.

command.name: Command
command.description: Door-open command. Empty = the one of the phonebook's door actuator for that panel, otherwise OPEN_2F.

fetch_local.name: Local HTTP fetch
fetch_local.description: GET (Digest sipID/password) to the intercom's local web interface. Admins only.

host.name: Host
host.description: Private or loopback IP (default: the intercom)

find_sga.name: Find SGA/PICG
find_sga.description: Sends GET_NICKS (Panda: blue) to the given addresses one at a time and stops when the intercom answers with GET_NICKS_REPLY: the entry with role PICG is the system's group head. Use it when you don't know the SGA and have no phonebook (cloud-only systems, issue #14). On the reference system GET_NICKS raises no notification in the app; on others this is not verified yet. It does not change the configuration unless you choose Apply.

end.name: Last address
end.description: End of the range (inclusive). At most 50 addresses.

targets.name: Specific addresses
targets.description: Instead of the range, a comma-separated list (e.g. 55001, 55002, 55100). If set, start/end are ignored.

delay.name: Pause between probes
delay.description: Seconds between one probe and the next.

reply_wait.name: Reply wait
reply_wait.description: Seconds to wait for GET_NICKS_REPLY after each accepted probe.

apply.name: Apply as PICG
apply.description: If found, write it to picg_target (the integration reloads).

apply_sga.name: Also apply as SGA
apply_sga.description: If found, also write the same address to sga_target (target of voicemail, do-not-disturb and door opening). They matched on every system seen so far, but they are two distinct values.

probe.name: Probe
probe.description: get_nicks (default) raises no notification in the app and its reply names the PICG. get_init_status is the fallback for systems where get_nicks times out: it gives the three clean outcomes, but sent to the real SGA it makes the app show "Configurazione appartamento modificata" every time.

sip_timeout.name: SIP timeout per probe
sip_timeout.description: How long to wait for each probe's SIP answer (200/202/404) before moving on. Over the cloud the relay may answer 202 (accepted, not delivered) only after ~15 s, so use 20.

options.auto: Automatic (2 Mbit/s locally, 256 kbit/s over the cloud)

door_busy.message: Door not opened: another door command is still in progress

door_queued.message: Door not confirmed: the relay queued the command (202) and no device confirmed it

door_unconfirmed.message: No confirmation from the relay: the door may still open, wait before trying again

door_not_registered.message: Door not opened: the intercom is not registered

door_timeout.message: Door not opened: no answer from the intercom

door_error.message: Door not opened: the intercom answered with SIP error {code}

door_send_failed.message: Door not opened: the command could not be sent

command_queued.message: Command not confirmed: the relay queued it (202) and no device confirmed it

test_ring_busy.message: Test ring not started: a call is already in progress

vm_timeout_not_allowed.message: Value not allowed by the intercom: {option}

registration_refused.title: The intercom refuses Home Assistant's registration
registration_refused.description:
The intercom answers **{code}** to every registration of “{title}”: the credentials from the pairing QR are no longer valid. This happens when Home Assistant's slot on the intercom was regenerated or removed, for example while pairing another phone. Until then the intercom does not ring in Home Assistant, and video, door and voicemail do not work.

On the intercom, create a new QR for Home Assistant and in Home Assistant open the Vimar Intercom integration and choose **⋮ → Reconfigure** to paste it (entities and automations stay). The integration keeps retrying meanwhile: this notice goes away by itself as soon as the registration succeeds.
